chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yahya al-Lahham, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a free woman and for him is a slave wife, and the free woman did not know that for him is a slave wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the free woman desires to stay with the slave wife, she stays; and if she desires, she goes back to her family.'

I said to him: 'If she is not pleased with that and goes back to her family, is there a way for him upon her when she is not pleased with staying?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no way for him upon her when she is not pleased when she comes to know.'

I said: 'So her going back to her family is her divorce?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. When she goes out from his house, she observes a waiting period of three months or three menses-free periods, then she marries if she desires.'

key_terms.سَبِيلٌ: Authority/way (specifically the husband's right to keep her)
key_terms.قُرُوءٌ: Menstrual periods (used to calculate waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a free wife if her husband has a slave wife and she chooses to leave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of *Khiyar al-Nafadh* (option of separation) for a free wife upon discovering her husband's concurrent marriage to a slave girl, a ruling rooted in the preservation of her social status (*kafa'ah*). It clarifies that her voluntary departure from the marital home constitutes an irrevocable divorce (*Talaq*) rather than a mere separation, mandating a specific *Iddah* period of three months or three menstrual cycles before she may remarry, reflecting the jurisprudential nuance between free and enslaved women in Shia fiqh.
